description: We are a team of students passionate about space, science, technology and protecting our oceans. Our project, SeaNASA UAE, aims to use NASA satellite data to explore changes in the Arabian Gulf and raise awareness about marine conservation. We welcome creative and motivated team members interested in Python programming, data analysis, research, app development, design and presenting ideas. Let's explore Earth and make a difference together!
summary: What if we could make Earth’s hidden changes visible and turn satellite data into a powerful tool for understanding our planet? Dancing with the SARs is an interactive web application inspired by NASA’s NISAR mission, designed to make Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) technology easier to explore, understand, and use. Through an interactive global map, users can select locations around the world, investigate different types of surface changes, including ground movement, forest and vegetation changes, wetlands, flooding, and glacier movement, and search NASA’s Earthdata catalog for available NISAR observations. The application also introduces important radar concepts, such as backscatter, interferometric coherence, and surface displacement, helping users understand how satellites can reveal information about Earth’s surface during both day and night and through clouds. Our project transforms complex satellite science into an accessible, engaging experience that encourages curiosity, exploration, and scientific thinking. By connecting NASA’s powerful Earth observation technology with real-world environmental questions, Dancing with the SARs aims to inspire the next generation of innovators to understand our changing planet and use space-based science to help build a more sustainable future.
details: Dancing with the SARs is an interactive web application inspired by NASA’s NISAR mission, designed to help people explore how Earth’s surface changes over time using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) technology. The application works as an interactive Earth observation explorer where users can select any location on a global map, choose a research theme, such as ground movement, forest and vegetation changes, wetlands and flooding, or glaciers and ice, and search NASA’s Earthdata catalog for available NISAR observations within a selected date range. It also includes an educational section explaining radar concepts such as backscatter, interferometric coherence, and surface displacement, helping users understand how radar signals reveal information about our planet. The main benefits are making complex satellite science easier to understand, encouraging independent investigation, and helping users discover satellite observations relevant to environmental changes and natural processes. Our intended impact is to encourage students, researchers, and the public to become more interested in Earth observation and use scientific information to better understand environmental challenges. To develop the project, we used HTML to structure the application, CSS to create its visual design, and JavaScript to build its interactive features and functions. We also used Leaflet to create the interactive global map, NASA GIBS for the satellite-based map background, and NASA’s Common Metadata Repository (CMR) API to search for NISAR collection and observation metadata. No additional hardware was required. What makes our project creative is the idea of turning radar observations into a journey of exploration, where users can choose their own location and research question instead of simply reading information about satellites. The dancing theme represents the continuous movement and transformation of Earth’s surface. Our team considered accessibility, user experience, scientific accuracy, global coverage, different environmental applications, and the importance of clearly explaining what the available satellite data can and cannot show. We also designed the interface with a modern NASA-inspired appearance using dark navy, turquoise, and gold details to make scientific exploration engaging and easy to navigate.
